about: Explicit fixture snapshots for the Academic Reviewer design, with provenance. They are illustrative design scenarios, not canonical application data or service contracts. The React app keeps its current shared world; where it differs, keep the app’s facts and reproduce the layout (common/03).
fixtureSource: project/RV.dc.html, class Component static getters COURSES, SCOPES, TIMES, REC, RB and REFS, extracted verbatim by checks/harness/extract_fixtures.js

SUB-0086.name: Flash Distillation
SUB-0086.summary: Flash a hot binary feed across a valve into a drum and find the vapour fraction from your own readings.
SUB-0086.desc: Learners set the feed temperature and the drum pressure, read the vapour and liquid flows, and compare the vapour fraction with an equilibrium calculation.

WEB.browser: A current browser on a laptop or desktop

SUB-0071.summary: Calibrate a Venturi meter against a weigh tank and find its discharge coefficient.
SUB-0071.desc: Learners vary the flow, read the throat and inlet pressures and the collected mass, and plot the discharge coefficient against the Reynolds number.

UPD-0005.name: Distillation Column

live.t: Learners start a binary column from cold and bring it to steady state. They then change the reflux ratio and watch the overhead purity respond with realistic lag.
the reflux ratio raises the overhead purity, at the cost of more reboiler heat.

prop.t: Learners start a binary column from cold and bring it to steady state. They then change the reflux ratio and watch the overhead purity respond with realistic lag.
the reflux ratio raises the overhead purity, at the cost of more reboiler heat.

UPD-0005.why: Corrects the reflux statement in the description: raising the reflux ratio raises overhead purity — v1.2 says the opposite. The web link moves to build 1.3, which carries the same correction in its on-screen notes.
UPD-0005.summary: Bring a binary column from cold start to steady state, tuning reflux ratio against overhead purity under realistic lag.

SUB-0077.name: Conduction Through a Composite Wall
SUB-0077.summary: Measure the temperature profile across a three-layer wall and compare it with the series-resistance model.
SUB-0077.desc: Learners build a wall from three layers — brick, insulation and plaster — set the hot-side and cold-side temperatures, and read the temperature at each interface. They compare the measured profile and heat flux with the series thermal-resistance model and explain where the two differ.

WEB.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with a keyboard and mouse

VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Composite Wall Lab”. On first launch, set the play-area boundary.

unchangedByRefinement: The FINAL complete-role design uses exactly these fixtures. On 20 Oct 2026 the extraction from the refined component and from the completed role were compared and were identical; the refinement and the later internal-ID correction changed presentation only. Record IDs are still carried in the data and the routes; they are no longer printed in reviewer-facing labels.
